lines.text: We met in Hobb's kiln yard. Hobb himself was sitting on a floor in the upper city, watching my brother breathe.
Ilse in Cell Nine. Maric's cure somewhere below her. And the Order's wall in the tunnels, between us and both.
Every great house keeps two sets of books. The Order keeps three. Bread for Cell Nine. Coal for the halls. And ice, cartloads of it, every week, for the lowest level of all.
Then the people of Ashby stepped into the firelight. For two years, they had scrubbed the Order's floors and washed its robes.
Nobody looks at a laundress, my lord. We know when the guards change, and which doors stick. And we have robes.
And I know the passwords. They change every moon, and nobody ever lowers their voice in front of the junior Measurers.
Tobin's crate sat open beside her. A dozen fog lanterns, oiled and ready. Just in case, he had said.
Oswin was on his feet before anyone could stop him, bandaged from neck to waist.
Don't. I've been burned worse. By your brother, actually, two days ago.
I lost you the boon. I'm not losing Ilse too.
For three nights, Hobb's brickmakers had been taking the Order's wall apart from behind, brick by brick, leaving only its face standing.
The rest would stand on street corners from the cathedral to my father's door, pretending to be drunk. If anything went wrong, I would feel it.
We go in through the water. The same water the Order stole from the Lowmarket for twenty years.
Then a horse came into the yard, and every brickmaker froze. The rider in the plain grey cloak was Mirelle.
She looked at the robes, the lanterns, the chalk map on the kiln wall.
I came to see how Wren was. She looks well. I'm terrible at maps, by the way. Can't read a single one.
If you come back, Wren, tell me what's really down there. And if you don't, I was never here.
She rode out without looking back. It was the most helpful thing a princess has ever done for me.
The laundresses had brought robes for everyone. Oswin put his on and looked down at himself.
I look like a disappointed owl.
Three nights later, at the turn of the guard, we went down into the water.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-four, coming soon.
